findings.summary: The supplied probabilistic argument proves the simultaneous lower and upper bounds on all projections and the resulting ratio bound, uniformly over arbitrary finite unit-vector families.

The supplied collinear construction proves the stated simultaneous distortion bound B(M,m), including the grid-spacing estimate, Gaussian-tail calculation, and exact reduction of normalized rank-one distortion to scalar mean-square error.

The codebook formula is explicit once a suitable vector v is supplied, but v is obtained only existentially by the probabilistic method; no deterministic algorithm, complexity bound, finite-precision analysis, or efficient explicit construction is established.
Assuming the supplied Gaussian rate-distortion converse, the rank-one water-filling calculation and distortion bound prove 0≤Π_n(U,M)≤(1/(2n))log_2(M^2B(M,m)) whenever B(M,m)<1.
The asymptotic estimates prove that for M_n=ceil(2^{nR}) and ln|U_n|=o(n), B(M_n,|U_n|)=o(1), log_2(M_n^2B)=o(n), and consequently Π_n(U_n,M_n) tends to zero.

The corollary is valid for a prescribed subexponential family fixed independently of the codebook. It does not exclude exponentially large or continuous orientation families, codebook-dependent adversaries, higher-rank metrics, or other incompatibility-based lower bounds.

The supplied evidence decides neither whether π(R_0) is positively bounded for some rate nor whether π(R)=0 for every fixed positive rate. The family-dependent collinear construction gives no new bound for the full positive-semidefinite trace-n metric class and does not improve 0≤π(R)≤R.
